title: Megure's Sealed Secret
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran) omitted by convention. Deviating slightly from that convention: Inspector Megure and Suzuki Sonoko ARE included as person nodes here, because unlike a typical episode this two-parter's B-plot is literally Megure's own 20-years-earlier backstory (title: 'Megure's Sealed Secret') and Sonoko is directly targeted as a mistaken-identity near-victim whose escape/rescue drives the climax -- both carry unique plot facts beyond generic presence. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved, sharing an `order` integer. Multigraph: e.g. Sadakane->Aizawa carries both `kills` and `has_motive_against`. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep217-218_megures_sealed_secret.json) got the culprit right (Sadakane) but was thin: it compressed all three non-fatal attacks and the murder into one generic 'e3' event, used only a generic `knows` edge for every suspect-victim relationship, never captured the actual deduction mechanism (the platform-boots height-correction clue that clears owner Haruyoshi and the shoe-swap staging clue), and omitted entirely both the Sonoko near-victim subplot and Megure's own 20-year-old hit-and-run backstory that gives the episode its title and explains why he resisted using decoys. No `label.murderer_id` change was needed -- Sadakane is confirmed correct against the transcript. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Aizawa Tae and the other three attacked women all wore ganguro/yamanba fashion, which is always paired with platform boots -- but Tae's body was found in ordinary pumps that didn't even fit her feet, revealing someone swapped her shoes post-mortem to hide the platform-boot pattern connecting the attacks.

Survivors Mizutani and Ishiguro each said the attacker was 'about their own height' -- but that was while they themselves wore platform boots (~10cm lift); measured barefoot at the station days later, they were only 151cm and 153cm. Correcting for the boots means the true culprit is roughly 10cm taller than the ~150cm first assumed, ruling out the ~150cm-tall store owner Haruyoshi and pointing instead to guard Sadakane's true 167cm.
